title: Establish a typed portfolio content layer and deterministic universe-signal placement without adding a CMS runtime

scope.subject: Personal content ingestion, validation, automatic galaxy placement, and world-level signal presentation

research_summary: The universe backbone is now stable enough to accept real portfolio content. Astro 7 already includes build-time Content Collections with glob/file loaders, Zod 4 schemas and typed queries, so local content can be validated and serialized into the existing React island without another runtime. Keystatic, TinaCMS and Decap provide useful editing UIs, but each adds admin/config/auth or rendering integration that does not improve the visitor experience yet. Select Astro Content Collections as the canonical storage/query layer, keep Keystatic compatible as a later editor, and attach sparse personal content as deterministic signal overlays to existing YEIS stars/worlds rather than fabricating content for every procedural planet.

sources.finding: Astro 7 Content Collections provide built-in glob() and file() loaders, Zod schema validation, typed getCollection/getEntry queries, and support custom/remote loaders.
Keystatic integrates with Astro and can manage Markdown/Markdoc content files while examples query them through Astro Content Collections, making it a compatible optional editor later.
TinaCMS provides first-class Astro visual editing but existing-site setup adds Tina packages and commonly SSR adapter/island plumbing, broader than needed for the current static content substrate.
Decap CMS provides a Git-backed browser editor but requires an admin surface and backend/auth configuration while frontend content usage remains the site's responsibility.

search_ladder.conclusion: Multiple full CMS/editor solutions exist, but their extra admin/runtime/auth surfaces solve authoring convenience rather than the immediate visitor-facing content substrate.
The existing Astro + React/R3F shell can receive serialized content as island props and render signals without a second frontend framework.
Astro Content Collections cover typed ingestion while the selected YEIS backbone already supplies stable astronomical anchors for deterministic content signals.
Built-in glob loader, Zod schema and getCollection query primitives cover the individual loading/validation pieces without custom parsing packages.

coverage_matrix.capability: typed local content schema and build-time validation
coverage_matrix.decision: Use Astro's already-installed content layer as the canonical schema/query substrate.

coverage_matrix.capability: zero additional visitor runtime and static deployment
coverage_matrix.decision: The content substrate should compile to plain serialized island props; editing UI is not part of the visitor bundle.
Keep content as ordinary repository files so Keystatic or another editor can be layered on later if authoring friction warrants it.

coverage_matrix.capability: deterministic automatic placement onto existing universe
coverage_matrix.decision: Placement belongs to the product adapter because CMS products manage content, not the semantics of YEIS stars and worlds.

coverage_matrix.capability: avoid fabricated personal history while scaling the universe
coverage_matrix.decision: Store only real authored entries; all unassigned worlds remain astronomical/procedural rather than receiving synthetic biography text.

candidates.name: Astro Content Collections + deterministic YEIS signal placement
candidates.source: Astro built-in content layer plus the existing YEIS adapter
candidates.license: MIT Astro; project-owned content; existing YEIS data/source notices unchanged
candidates.reason: Uses capabilities already shipped in the installed framework, adds no visitor runtime or CMS service, preserves static deployment, and leaves content files compatible with a later Git editor.

candidates.name: Install Keystatic now as the canonical content authoring layer
candidates.reason: Good future editor and compatible with file-based Astro content, but adds packages/config/admin UI before there is evidence that direct file authoring is a bottleneck.

candidates.name: Install TinaCMS and visual editing as the content foundation
candidates.reason: Visual editing is powerful but the required integration surface is much larger than the single-owner static portfolio currently needs and would couple deployment choices to authoring.

candidates.name: Add Decap CMS admin and Git backend before content modeling
candidates.reason: Mature and lightweight for editors, but still adds an exposed admin/auth/backend workflow and does not solve universe placement; that is negative global value for the current single-owner phase.

decision.rationale: Use Astro's built-in typed content layer as the canonical source and add only a narrow deterministic placement adapter that maps real entries to existing YEIS stars/worlds. Keep editing products optional and future-compatible instead of introducing a CMS runtime before it provides measurable value.

higher_level_tradeoffs.reason: Keystatic is broader because it adds a full editor, but current value is lower: the repository has one owner and Astro already handles storage/query/schema. Its file compatibility means postponing it does not create migration debt.

TinaCMS offers broader visual editing, but its extra packages, admin surface and server/island integration increase deployment and runtime complexity without improving current visitor-facing content placement.
Decap adds a complete Git-based admin workflow, but authentication/backend setup and an exposed admin surface are unnecessary now, while universe placement still must be implemented locally.

decision.fallback: If file authoring becomes painful, add Keystatic on top of the same content directory/schema without changing the runtime placement API. If remote sources are later useful, Astro custom loaders can feed the same collection interface.
